problem_statement: Let C2: y^2 = x^6 - 3x^5 + x^4 + 3x^2 - x + 1 over Q (smooth, genus 2, leading coefficient a square, two points at infinity infinity-plus and infinity-minus). Naively visible affine points include (0,+/-1). With Jacobian rank 1 and p=13 a good Chabauty prime, prove via Coleman zero bound (including infinity disks) and Mordell-Weil sieve at 17 and 31 that C2(Q) equals exactly the naive finite set {infinity-plus, infinity-minus, (0,1), (0,-1)}.
